about.title: Personal Injury Help in Mammoth Lakes, California
about.longDescription: Mammoth Lakes is a small mountain town, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show reported crashes here tend to cluster on Thursdays between 4 and 6 p.m., with Rt 203, Main Street, Minaret Road, and Old Mammoth Road logging the highest volume of collision reports in town. The most recent finalized year on record showed zero reported traffic deaths and zero injury collisions countywide — a reassuring number, though incidents involving visitors, seasonal traffic, and winter road conditions still happen and can leave people hurt or shaken. If you were injured in or around Mammoth Lakes, whether from a vehicle collision, a slip on icy pavement, or another type of accident, you don't have to sort out the next steps on your own. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Mono County with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened. There's no cost to talk, and attorneys in this network only get paid if you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity — like a city road crew or transit agency — was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Disqualify You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover compensation — it's just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of a settlement or verdict — if there's no recovery, you owe nothing for their time.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Mammoth Lakes?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a public road maintained by the city or county, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen most in Mammoth Lakes?
items.answer: Based on public collision records, Rt 203, Main Street, Minaret Road, and Old Mammoth Road show the highest volume of reported crashes in town, with reports clustering most often on Thursdays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply public-record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is just reduced in proportion to your share of responsibility, and an attorney can help you understand how that might apply to your situation.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — in typical personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, or emotional distress. This is different from some other states, and it's one reason it can help to have a knowledgeable attorney evaluate your claim.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in Mono County, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning you don't pay legal fees unless they recover money for you.
